title: Structs, Methods & Interfaces Basics
intro: Structs and interfaces are Go's answer to classes and inheritance — and the interview question 'how does Go do OOP?' is one every Go fresher faces. This module covers struct definition and initialisation (named fields, positional literals, the zero-value struct), value receivers vs pointer receivers (when a method should take *T vs T, the rule of thumb: mutating methods take a pointer receiver, read-only methods can take either, but be consistent on a type), the method set rules (value T includes value-receiver methods; *T includes both), interfaces in Go (defining an interface with one or more method signatures), implicit satisfaction (a type satisfies an interface by having the right methods — no 'implements' keyword needed), and struct embedding as Go's composition mechanism. Every answer addresses the comparison to Java/Python classes that interviewers expect you to articulate: 'Go doesn't have inheritance — what does it have instead and why is that a good thing?'
